facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against calling the requested work ready is that the missing items are the ones a credit committee relies on: the covenant ratio with its definition of earnings, and the lien, guarantee and call terms in the executed debt documents. The revolver test springs only when loans exceed 35% of the USD 800 million commitments, so the test binds only once borrowings pass that level, but the definition of earnings decides when that point is reached, and a filing's summary can omit baskets and definitions. Any covenant or security conclusion should therefore stay conditional. Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Cash interest paid for the nine-month 2025 and 2026 periods, and therefore for the last twelve months, is not printed in the quarterly reports; it restricts cash-basis interest cover to full years and leaves the latest period without a measure. Severity High; the action that would close it is a release, presentation or note stating nine-month cash interest paid. - The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA and prints no covenant ratio, so the adjusted EBITDA row and the EBITDA bridge are not supplied and covenant headroom is not established; it restricts every leverage ratio to a constructed reported measure. Severity High; the action is the issuer's adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and the credit agreement's earnings definition. - Income taxes paid for the nine-month periods are not printed, so cash tax is available for full years only. Severity Low; the action is a note or release stating nine-month cash taxes. - The December 2023 revolver availability is not stated in the 2024 annual report, so undrawn committed facilities and liquidity for FY2023 are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the 2023 annual report. - The balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is not in any supplied filing, so the nine-month 2025 balance sheet column and any ratio on it are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the third-quarter 2025 report. - Nine months 2024 is not in the supplied filings, so nine-month 2025 revenue and EBITDA growth and the growth of the prior last twelve months are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the third-quarter 2025 report. - Several cash flow and income statement cells are printed as dashes, among them impairments, gain on sale of assets, loss on extinguishment of debt, inventory step-up amortization and financing costs, and several lines exist only in the annual or only in the interim statements; they are carried as not supplied rather than zero, and the printed totals add up with those cells at zero. Severity Low; no action is needed. - Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not disclosed, so only total capital expenditure is carried. Severity Low; the action is management's split of capital expenditure. - Debt is not split by seniority on the balance sheet and USD 91 million of other debt and failed sale-leaseback obligations carry no stated security, rank, rate or amortization schedule, so they are left out of the debt stack and out of senior secured subtotals. Severity Medium; the action is the credit agreement, indentures and lease documents. - The parent's own statements and debt are not in the supplied filings, so the parent's accounting basis and any parent-level leverage are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the parent's annual report. - Lease, pension and commitment figures exist only at 2025-12-31 because the quarterly reports carry no such notes, so the claims outside debt are nine months older than the debt figures. Severity Medium; the action is management's quarterly figures for these claims. - The carrying value of the euro floating rate notes in euro is not printed, only the US dollar translation, so the carrying value cell for that instrument is not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the issuer's euro carrying amount. - A discrete third-quarter income statement is printed but discrete quarters of depreciation and cash flow are not, so no discrete quarter is carried and nine-month columns stand in. Severity Low; the action is a release stating third-quarter depreciation and cash flow. - The payment date of the USD 75 million executive payment is not stated and the USD 85 million acquisition had not closed at the filing date, so the pro forma figures are single-event illustrations. Severity Medium; the action is the closing and payment disclosures after 2026-10-28. - Per-share data and weighted average share counts are printed but not carried in the statement tables because they are not monetary millions. Severity Low; no action is needed.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Control is the dominant risk and it is complete. Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, can elect the board, generally decides mergers, financing and dividend policy, and under the separation agreement the issuer needs its written consent for certain significant actions until the parent holds less than 50% of the votes; the issuer qualifies for controlled-company exemptions from board-independence rules. Creditors therefore cannot count on the board to resist the parent on strategy, distributions or acquisitions while control lasts, although related-party dealings need independent-director approval. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C1

facts.text: - The separation is open-ended and ownership can change on the parent's terms. A distribution depends on the parent reaching targeted debt leverage ratios that are not stated, the parent can terminate the distribution arrangement in its sole discretion, and the agreement's outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination. Part of the parent's holding sits in a subsidiary and is pledged for that subsidiary's own 10.00% senior secured notes due 2032, in an amount not stated, so a default there could put an unknown owner in control. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues since the listing have been refinancings. On 2022-05-10 the issuer took a USD 2,500 million term loan and a USD 500 million revolver; the term loan proceeds and cash paid the parent USD 2,429 million. It added USD 1,400 million of secured notes and USD 500 million of term loans on 2023-09-29 to buy XIIDRA and USD 400 million of term loans on 2024-11-01. On 2025-06-26 it replaced the 2027 maturities with a USD 800 million revolver due 2030, a USD 2,325 million term loan due 2031 and EUR 675 million of floating rate notes due 2031, and on 2026-01-02 it refinanced the 2028 and 2031 term loans into a USD 2,802 million term loan due 2031-01-15 to extend maturities and lower the rate. At 2026-09-30 principal outstanding was USD 5,065 million, or USD 5,017 million net of USD 48 million of unamortized discounts and issuance costs: the term loan USD 2,788 million, the 2028 notes USD 1,400 million, the 2031 notes USD 765 million, the revolver USD 100 million and other debt USD 12 million. The credit facilities and both note series are secured by the same first-priority liens, the notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement and carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control, and the revolver has a springing first lien net leverage test of 5.75x stepping down to 5.00x that applies only when more than 35% of the USD 800 million commitments are drawn. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 258; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 191–192; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C33

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Leverage has fallen but remains high, and it fell because earnings rose, not because debt fell. Total debt of USD 5,095 million is 6.47x last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 787 million, against 9.52x at FY2025, while debt itself is higher than at FY2025. EBITDA rose 47.38%, but USD 62 million of non-cash inventory step-up amortization sat in the FY2025 base, so the like-for-like rise is 32.05%. Because leverage is a ratio to one year of earnings, a return of EBITDA to its FY2025 level, a fall of 32.15%, would put total debt at 9.54x EBITDA. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital spending is the main flexible cash item, but its flexibility is not established. The issuer lists about USD 60 million of capital spending for the fourth quarter and had capital commitments of USD 128 million at year-end 2025, and it does not split maintenance from growth spending. The receivables sale facility signed in January 2026 produced only USD 26 million of proceeds in nine months, all collected by quarter-end, so it is a small and optional source of liquidity and not a driver of the cash flow shown. Cash available for debt reduction after interest is therefore limited to the last-twelve-month free cash flow, and the term loan amortization is only USD 28 million a year, so deleveraging has to come from earnings growth. Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed charges: operating lease liabilities of USD 163 million and a net pension and retiree deficit of USD 31 million at 2025-12-31 sit outside total debt, while USD 78 million of failed sale-leaseback obligations sit inside it. facts.text: The financial profile is weak and improving, and the business profile is average. facts.text: The financial transmission is through leverage and cover before liquidity. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Bausch + Lomb presents an adequate business profile supported by a three-segment product range, repeat consumer and clinician demand and growth in each of the last three years, but credit quality is constrained by total debt of 6.47x EBITDA, thin interest cover, a mostly floating debt structure and control by a parent with a pledged stake. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but unproven: free cash flow of USD 252 million is one year old and rests on pricing and a depressed 2025 base. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings holding above USD 787 million, on rebates staying contained and on the parent not taking cash or losing control before the 2028 notes mature. Business quality compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers in eye health is not established, because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require cash interest paid for 2026, the credit agreement and covenant definitions, the size of the pledge and Lumify revenue. ## Request

Bausch & Lomb Corp (reporting as Bausch + Lomb Corporation and its subsidiaries; issuer id blco-1860742), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the five supplied filings can support the requested modules (Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit) and what the wider pathway still lacks. The run settings are context, not evidence.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2024 | 2025-02-19 | d1a818e6dae62c0569001be3adf70a8440ab09b135fbd8a8415d916f347ac944 | Audited statements for 2022 to 2024, year-end 2024 debt table and ratings, and the check of 2024 comparatives against the 2025 annual report |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-18 | f9be8b58ba08e3778eb7929adfd8e91c7937b14763b1612985a5ea40049fae96 | Audited statements for 2023 to 2025, year-end 2025 debt table, leases, pensions, commitments, market-risk sensitivity and the business description |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_blco_blco-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-04-29 | b5fd820786b285fad91b4bbfc64c3e7e4ef0ef85e352ca3af624a2c65416917e | Unaudited first-quarter 2026 statements and the location of debt, covenant, liquidity and ratings text |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_blco_blco-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 | 2026-07-29 | 756a1d9122dd4fe39810dfb8ff6416d6377e3c912267a2effad38ff1ca21dc42 | Unaudited second-quarter and six-month 2026 statements and the location of debt, covenant, liquidity and ratings text |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-10-28 | 846d19ab6fa76521b0c1971958df2b6423a7a62d000b6bf115cb56f37aff87b9 | Latest statements, debt table, maturities, covenant text, liquidity, ratings, events after the quarter and all arithmetic checks |
Supplied handoffs from other modules: none; this module is the entry point of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The sources support a creditor view of Bausch + Lomb's debt, liquidity and operating results to 2026-09-30, but not of covenant headroom or security terms, so leverage must be computed from the statements and legal conclusions stay conditional.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 71

The debt table, the maturity schedule and the balance sheet reconcile, with USD 5,065 million of principal outstanding at 2026-09-30. The newest filing is dated 2026-10-28, 21 days before the as-of date, so later events are not established. The three requested modules are ready with limitations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–38; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C10
### Key findings

- Coverage is sufficient for the requested work. Two audited annual reports and three unaudited quarterly reports of the issuer's own consolidated group give income statements and cash flows for 2022 to 2025 and for the nine months to 2026-09-30 with 2025 comparatives, so the last twelve months can be built from the filings and the fourth quarter of 2025 by subtraction.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 225–227; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 235–237; 10-Q_2026-03-31_blco_blco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_blco_blco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

- Debt and liquidity inputs are printed in full in the third-quarter report: a table by instrument showing USD 5,065 million of principal, a maturity schedule that sums to the same figure, and a revolver with USD 666 million of availability after USD 100 million of borrowings and USD 34 million of letters of credit.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5

- The reporting entity is the issuer's own consolidated group, not its parent. Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, but the statements supplied are the issuer's, so parent-level debt and support are not established by these sources.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

- Leverage and covenant headroom cannot be taken from the issuer. No filing prints a figure for EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or free cash flow, the only adjusted measure being constant-currency revenue, and the revolver's springing first lien net leverage test is printed as thresholds of 5.75x stepping down to 5.00x that apply only when loans exceed 35% of commitments, with compliance stated but no ratio.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

- Claims outside the debt figure are only partly current. Operating lease liabilities of USD 163 million at 2025-12-31 sit outside the balance-sheet debt lines, USD 34 million of failed sale-leaseback obligations sit inside them and had grown to USD 78 million by 2026-09-30, and capital commitments were about USD 128 million at 2025-12-31. The quarterly reports carry no lease or pension note, so these items are nine months older than the debt table. A receivables sale arrangement raised USD 26 million in the nine months and nothing was outstanding at 2026-09-30.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 296–297; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 319; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8

- The third-quarter report discloses events after the period that its statements do not reflect: an acquisition agreement with about USD 85 million of upfront cash expected at closing, and a chief executive change with a lump-sum payment of about USD 75 million. It also states fourth-quarter 2026 cash needs, including about USD 130 million of interest. Nothing dated after 2026-10-28 is supplied, so the 21 days to the as-of date are not covered.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; calculation C10

- The sources agree wherever they overlap. The 2024 comparatives in the 2025 annual report equal the 2024 annual report, and the December 2025 comparatives in the third-quarter report equal the 2025 annual report, so no restatement of totals or conflict was found. The differences found are presentation only: the debt line now reads "and other financial liabilities", a discounts-and-allowances line is folded into other accrued liabilities, and acquisition-related contingent consideration is split out of the cash-flow Other line with the subtotals unchanged.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 225–227; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 235–237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 280; calculation C6

- Legal and market inputs for structure and pricing are missing. No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, and the filings only summarise the financing documents. They give an aggregate fair value of debt of USD 5,091 million at 2026-09-30 and name an equity peer group, but no instrument-level quote, valuation or peer financials, so Legal & covenants, Security selection and Recovery & fulcrum would be conditional on those documents.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 157

- Ratings and outlooks of three agencies are printed as of 2026-10-28 although the run supplies none; the Moody's row shows one rating only, so whether it is the corporate or the secured rating is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 88
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against calling the requested work ready is that the missing items are the ones a credit committee relies on: the covenant ratio with its definition of earnings, and the lien, guarantee and call terms in the executed debt documents. The revolver test springs only when loans exceed 35% of the USD 800 million commitments, so the test binds only once borrowings pass that level, but the definition of earnings decides when that point is reached, and a filing's summary can omit baskets and definitions. Any covenant or security conclusion should therefore stay conditional.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C5

The view would improve to ready for Legal & covenants and Covenant capacity if the credit agreement and the indentures were supplied, and for Earnings changes and Earnings quality if a third-quarter earnings release or lender presentation printing adjusted EBITDA were supplied. It would weaken if a filing dated after 2026-10-28 restated figures, closed the acquisition on different terms or changed the revolver.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

## Request

Bausch & Lomb Corp (reporting as Bausch + Lomb Corporation and its subsidiaries; issuer id blco-1860742), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the issuer's financial foundation from the five supplied filings, namely statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage to 2026-09-30. Figures are in US dollars; the run settings are context, not evidence.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage fell to 6.47x total debt and 5.82x net debt to LTM reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, from 9.52x and 8.80x at FY2025, but cash interest cover cannot be measured for the latest twelve months, so the improvement is unproven against debt service.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 235–236; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 308; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C13

The improvement comes from USD 253 million more LTM EBITDA, not from debt reduction, because total debt rose to USD 5,095 million from USD 5,082 million. FY2025 cash interest cover was 1.41x. Cash and revolver availability of USD 1,179 million cover the fourth-quarter cash needs the company states, about USD 357 million, and nothing but amortization falls due before 2028. Net leverage would be 5.93x after the acquisition or 5.92x after the executive payment announced after the quarter.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C25; calculation C28; calculation C31; calculation C35; calculation C39; calculation C40
### Key findings

- Leverage fell because earnings rose, not because debt fell. Reported EBITDA, which the issuer does not state and which is built here as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, was USD 787 million for the last twelve months against USD 534 million for FY2025, while total debt moved from USD 5,082 million to USD 5,095 million. Nine-month operating income was USD 271 million against USD 1 million a year earlier, on revenue of USD 4,013 million against USD 3,696 million, and USD 62 million of non-cash inventory step-up amortization sat in the 2025 comparison period while the 2026 statement prints none, so about USD 62 million of the rise is the end of a non-cash charge and not operating improvement.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 235–236; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 237–238; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C13; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C55; calculation C60

- Coverage is thin and only partly measurable. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 1.41x in FY2025, 1.44x in FY2024 and 2.15x in FY2023, but cash interest paid is printed only in the annual reports, so the latest twelve months cannot be measured on the method's cash basis. On accrued interest expense, which the quarterly statements do print, LTM EBITDA covers USD 383 million of expense 2.05x against 1.27x in FY2025; that is a labelled proxy, not the method's measure.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 308; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 235–236; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C18

- Cash conversion improved with earnings. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 418 million against USD 147 million and capital expenditure fell to USD 226 million from USD 273 million, so free cash flow was USD 192 million against negative USD 126 million, and LTM free cash flow is USD 252 million after annual deficits of USD 198 million in FY2023, USD 59 million in FY2024 and USD 66 million in FY2025. Operating cash flow was 72.57% of nine-month reported EBITDA against 45.51% a year earlier, and capital expenditure was 5.63% of nine-month revenue against 7.39%.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 237–238; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C22; calculation C19; calculation C49; calculation C48

- Liquidity covers the stated near-term needs. Cash of USD 513 million plus USD 666 million of revolver availability, after USD 100 million of borrowings and USD 34 million of letters of credit, is USD 1,179 million against USD 1,047 million at FY2025. The company states fourth-quarter 2026 cash needs of about USD 357 million, being interest of about USD 130 million, amortization of USD 7 million, capital expenditure of about USD 60 million, the USD 85 million acquisition and the USD 75 million executive payment, so liquidity is about 3.30x those needs.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C31; calculation C32

- The debt is back-ended. The four main instruments are senior secured and rank equally. Nothing falls due before 2028 beyond amortization; USD 1,440 million falls due in 2028, led by the 2028 secured notes of USD 1,400 million, and USD 3,434 million falls due in 2031, being the term loan balance and the euro notes. The weighted average stated interest rate is 7.63% and the revolver of USD 800 million matures in 2030.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 191–194; calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C38

- Reported EBITDA is unadjusted. It carries USD 127 million of other expense, net over the last twelve months, including restructuring, litigation, acquired research and contingent-consideration charges. Adding that back, a house sensitivity labelled Analyst Judgement and applied in no ratio, would lift LTM EBITDA to USD 914 million and cut total leverage to 5.57x. The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA, so no issuer-adjusted figure or bridge exists to show beside it.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 303; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C54; calculation C41; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Total debt of USD 5,095 million is balance-sheet carrying value and includes USD 78 million of failed sale-leaseback obligations. Contractual principal is USD 5,065 million, so carrying value is USD 30 million higher: USD 78 million of other financial liabilities less USD 48 million of unamortized discount. Operating lease liabilities of USD 163 million and a net pension and retiree deficit of USD 31 million at 2025-12-31 sit outside debt and are in no ratio here.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 292–297; calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C42

- Two events after 2026-09-30 would raise net debt of USD 4,582 million: USD 85 million of upfront cash for the acquisition of surgical manufacturing businesses, giving USD 4,667 million or 5.93x, and the USD 75 million lump-sum payment to the departing chief executive, giving USD 4,657 million or 5.92x. Neither is in the period figures; the filing describes the acquisition as expected to close in the fourth quarter, and it does not state when the payment is made.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; calculation C4; calculation C39; calculation C40

- The material gaps are cash interest paid for the interim periods, any issuer-stated adjusted EBITDA, and a stated rank for USD 91 million of other debt-like items left out of the debt stack. Covenant headroom is not established because the issuer prints no covenant ratio.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C37
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that leverage has not truly improved is that the gain is a nine-month figure measured against a 2025 base that carried USD 62 million of step-up amortization, that total debt is higher than at FY2025, and that cash interest, the real debt-service test, is unmeasured for the latest period. Cash interest paid has differed from accrued expense by USD 16 million to USD 45 million in each of the last three years, in both directions, so the proxy of 2.05x is a guide and not a measure.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 308; calculation C55; calculation C26; calculation C21; calculation C56

The view would strengthen if fourth-quarter results keep LTM EBITDA at or above USD 787 million, and if the USD 85 million acquisition and the USD 75 million payment are funded from cash without a revolver draw. It would weaken if nine-month cash interest paid proves far above the proxy, or if the issuer's own covenant definition of earnings gives a lower figure than reported EBITDA.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C13; calculation C39; calculation C40
### Limitations

- Reported EBITDA is constructed from operating income and the depreciation and amortization line of the cash flow statement; the issuer defines no EBITDA, so every ratio here depends on that construction and on no add-backs.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- Cash interest paid, income taxes paid, leases and pensions are printed only for full years, so interim and latest-twelve-month cash coverage cannot be built and year-end 2025 claims are dated nine months before the latest debt figures.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 308; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 296–297
- Nine-month columns stand in for the discrete quarters; a discrete third-quarter income statement is printed but its cash flows and depreciation are not, so no discrete quarter is carried.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17
- Pro forma figures after 2026-09-30 are single-event illustrations from stated amounts, not cumulative and not a forecast.

## Gaps

- Cash interest paid for the nine-month 2025 and 2026 periods, and therefore for the last twelve months, is not printed in the quarterly reports; it restricts cash-basis interest cover to full years and leaves the latest period without a measure. Severity High; the action that would close it is a release, presentation or note stating nine-month cash interest paid.

- The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA and prints no covenant ratio, so the adjusted EBITDA row and the EBITDA bridge are not supplied and covenant headroom is not established; it restricts every leverage ratio to a constructed reported measure. Severity High; the action is the issuer's adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and the credit agreement's earnings definition.
- Income taxes paid for the nine-month periods are not printed, so cash tax is available for full years only. Severity Low; the action is a note or release stating nine-month cash taxes.

- The December 2023 revolver availability is not stated in the 2024 annual report, so undrawn committed facilities and liquidity for FY2023 are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the 2023 annual report.

- The balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is not in any supplied filing, so the nine-month 2025 balance sheet column and any ratio on it are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the third-quarter 2025 report.

- Nine months 2024 is not in the supplied filings, so nine-month 2025 revenue and EBITDA growth and the growth of the prior last twelve months are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the third-quarter 2025 report.

- Several cash flow and income statement cells are printed as dashes, among them impairments, gain on sale of assets, loss on extinguishment of debt, inventory step-up amortization and financing costs, and several lines exist only in the annual or only in the interim statements; they are carried as not supplied rather than zero, and the printed totals add up with those cells at zero. Severity Low; no action is needed.
- Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not disclosed, so only total capital expenditure is carried. Severity Low; the action is management's split of capital expenditure.

- Debt is not split by seniority on the balance sheet and USD 91 million of other debt and failed sale-leaseback obligations carry no stated security, rank, rate or amortization schedule, so they are left out of the debt stack and out of senior secured subtotals. Severity Medium; the action is the credit agreement, indentures and lease documents.

- The parent's own statements and debt are not in the supplied filings, so the parent's accounting basis and any parent-level leverage are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the parent's annual report.

- Lease, pension and commitment figures exist only at 2025-12-31 because the quarterly reports carry no such notes, so the claims outside debt are nine months older than the debt figures. Severity Medium; the action is management's quarterly figures for these claims.

- The carrying value of the euro floating rate notes in euro is not printed, only the US dollar translation, so the carrying value cell for that instrument is not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the issuer's euro carrying amount.

- A discrete third-quarter income statement is printed but discrete quarters of depreciation and cash flow are not, so no discrete quarter is carried and nine-month columns stand in. Severity Low; the action is a release stating third-quarter depreciation and cash flow.

- The payment date of the USD 75 million executive payment is not stated and the USD 85 million acquisition had not closed at the filing date, so the pro forma figures are single-event illustrations. Severity Medium; the action is the closing and payment disclosures after 2026-10-28.
- Per-share data and weighted average share counts are printed but not carried in the statement tables because they are not monetary millions. Severity Low; no action is needed.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Control by Bausch Health, which holds about 87% of the shares and supplies the chairman and interim chief executive, is the main non-financial risk for creditors, because ownership can change through a distribution, sale or foreclosure. The business is diversified across three segments, the issuer has paid no dividend since 2022, and the only debt-funded transfer to the parent in the filings is the USD 2,429 million paid at the listing, funded by new term debt and cash.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 157–158; 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 258; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation C1; calculation C33

Operating risk is secondary: Surgical earned USD 18 million of segment profit in 2025 against USD 50 million in 2023, and rebates took 39.5% of gross product sales. The view worsens if the parent draws cash out or control passes to an unknown holder.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; calculation C37
### Key findings

- Control is the dominant risk and it is complete. Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, can elect the board, generally decides mergers, financing and dividend policy, and under the separation agreement the issuer needs its written consent for certain significant actions until the parent holds less than 50% of the votes; the issuer qualifies for controlled-company exemptions from board-independence rules. Creditors therefore cannot count on the board to resist the parent on strategy, distributions or acquisitions while control lasts, although related-party dealings need independent-director approval.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C1

- Leadership is now shared with the parent. The parent's chief executive has chaired the board since August 2026 and became interim chief executive on 2026-10-12, when the former chief executive left under an agreement paying about USD 75 million; the issuer itself names the time demands and conflicts of the dual role as a risk and states no permanent successor. Decisions on strategy, acquisitions and cash can now be taken by one person who answers to both companies.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104

- The separation is open-ended and ownership can change on the parent's terms. A distribution depends on the parent reaching targeted debt leverage ratios that are not stated, the parent can terminate the distribution arrangement in its sole discretion, and the agreement's outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination. Part of the parent's holding sits in a subsidiary and is pledged for that subsidiary's own 10.00% senior secured notes due 2032, in an amount not stated, so a default there could put an unknown owner in control. Both secured notes give holders a repurchase right at 101% on a change of control; whether the credit agreement has an equivalent is not stated.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194

- The record of cash going to the parent is mixed and dated. In 2022 the issuer paid the parent USD 2,200 million to settle an intercompany note and USD 229 million as a return of capital, funded by the new term loan and cash. Since the listing no dividend has been declared or paid, the parent's agreements cost the issuer USD 8 million in 2025, no sales were made to related parties, and a 2022 lawsuit seeking to treat transfers from the parent as voidable and to make the issuer liable for damages awarded against the parent was settled in 2025 and dismissed in January 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 258; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 263–264; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 317–318; calculation C33

- The operating base is broad but concentrated at the edges. Revenue was USD 5,101 million in 2025, up 6.47%, across three segments, with 49.91% earned in the United States and Puerto Rico; yet the top ten products were 56% of revenue against 48% in 2023, two wholesalers are each about 10% of revenue, finished product for six named products comes from a single source, and about 37% of product sales are made wholly or partly by third parties.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 322–323; calculation C24; calculation C27

- Profit rests on Vision Care and on rebate discipline. Vision Care earned USD 849 million of the USD 1,125 million segment profit in 2025 at a 29.05% margin, while the Pharmaceuticals margin fell to 20.09% in 2025 from 28.83% in 2023, with rebates rising to 24.40% of gross product sales in 2025 from 19.90% in 2024, and recovered to 28.17% in the first nine months of 2026, when deductions eased. Surgical earned a 2.01% margin in 2025, in the year of the enVista recall, and 8.08% in the nine months of 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 169; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; calculation C6; calculation C11; calculation C16; calculation C14; calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C23; calculation C41

- Acquisitions since the 2023 purchase of XIIDRA have been small by comparison, and the pending one has no stated funding. XIIDRA cost USD 1,750 million upfront and was paid from the 2023 secured notes and term loan; deals since January 2025 total about USD 221 million of upfront cash including the pending USD 85 million purchase of surgical manufacturing businesses, whose target, size and funding source the filings do not state. Contingent payments of about USD 242 million are reasonably possible.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 269–270; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 320; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C35

- Disclosure supports monitoring of the issuer but not analysis of the parent. The statements are audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers with an unqualified opinion and effective internal control, and the one critical audit matter is the Medicaid rebate estimate, with USD 556 million of rebates accrued. Director, pay and related-person information is incorporated from a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the parent's own financial position, the size of the pledge and its leverage target are not stated.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 222; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 232; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 234–235; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Regulatory and quality events have so far been contained. The 2025 enVista recall was followed by a return to pre-recall sales in the fourth quarter of 2025, and the September 2026 FDA warning letter on the Tampa site does not require manufacturing to stop; management says it expects no supply interruption, a statement the filings do not test.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against putting control first is the parent's restraint since 2022. Its holding has not changed since 2025-02, no dividend has been paid, related-party dealings are small, the issuer refinanced on 2025-06-26 and 2026-01-02 to move maturities to January 2031, and the board has nine named independent directors with an auditor reporting effective controls. The debt is guaranteed by the issuer's own subsidiaries and the filings name no guarantee by the parent, so no contractual channel from the parent's debt to the issuer's is named in the filings, although ratings can move with the parent.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 263–264; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 191–192; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 232; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34

The view would improve if a distribution left no controlling shareholder, if a permanent chief executive independent of the parent were appointed, or if the pledge size and the parent's leverage target were disclosed and proved benign. It would worsen on a dividend, an intercompany loan or any other cash call by the parent, on a foreclosure on pledged shares, or on a sale to a holder whose plans differ, and on any rating action driven by the parent.

### Limitations

- The parent's own finances, the size of the pledge and the parent's leverage target are outside the five filings, so the likelihood and timing of an ownership change cannot be sized and the control conclusion stays qualitative.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Directors' backgrounds, committee membership, pay and the related-person policy sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the conclusion that creditors cannot count on the board to resist the parent rests on the controlled-company disclosure and a list of independent directors alone.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No single transaction sits at the centre of this credit. The open transaction is the separation from Bausch Health, announced on 2020-08-06 and not completed: a distribution depends on the parent reaching leverage targets that the filings do not state, the parent can end the arrangement at its sole discretion, the agreement's outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination, and a sale or a transfer to the parent's shareholders remains possible. No date is given.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

The one large acquisition since the listing was XIIDRA from Novartis, signed on 2023-06-30 and completed on 2023-09-29 for USD 1,750 million upfront plus potential milestones of up to USD 750 million, paid from USD 1,400 million of 8.375% secured notes due October 2028 and a new term loan. Later deals were small: Whitecap Biosciences for about USD 28 million on 2025-01-03, two acquisitions for about USD 33 million in November 2025 and Mexican manufacturing assets for about USD 75 million on 2025-12-09. On 2026-10-08 the issuer agreed to buy ophthalmic surgical manufacturing businesses for about USD 85 million of upfront cash, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026; the filings do not name the target, size it or state how the cash will be funded. The separation agreement with the former chief executive adds a lump-sum payment of about USD 75 million, payable under that agreement.

New debt issues since the listing have been refinancings. On 2022-05-10 the issuer took a USD 2,500 million term loan and a USD 500 million revolver; the term loan proceeds and cash paid the parent USD 2,429 million. It added USD 1,400 million of secured notes and USD 500 million of term loans on 2023-09-29 to buy XIIDRA and USD 400 million of term loans on 2024-11-01. On 2025-06-26 it replaced the 2027 maturities with a USD 800 million revolver due 2030, a USD 2,325 million term loan due 2031 and EUR 675 million of floating rate notes due 2031, and on 2026-01-02 it refinanced the 2028 and 2031 term loans into a USD 2,802 million term loan due 2031-01-15 to extend maturities and lower the rate. At 2026-09-30 principal outstanding was USD 5,065 million, or USD 5,017 million net of USD 48 million of unamortized discounts and issuance costs: the term loan USD 2,788 million, the 2028 notes USD 1,400 million, the 2031 notes USD 765 million, the revolver USD 100 million and other debt USD 12 million. The credit facilities and both note series are secured by the same first-priority liens, the notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement and carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control, and the revolver has a springing first lien net leverage test of 5.75x stepping down to 5.00x that applies only when more than 35% of the USD 800 million commitments are drawn.

Scope: the overall fundamental credit view, its strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside, drawn from the five supplied filings and the three earlier handoffs. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit quality is weak but improving: total debt of 6.47x last-twelve-month EBITDA, interest cover of 2.05x on accrued expense and control by Bausch Health leave creditors reliant on one year of earnings recovery holding until the 2028 maturities.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

The business is a three-segment eye-health franchise with revenue of USD 5,418 million over the last twelve months, and net pricing supplied 40.38% of the nine-month revenue increase. Liquidity of USD 1,179 million and no maturity beyond amortization before 2028 buy time, but net leverage of 5.82x at 2026-09-30 becomes 5.93x pro forma for the acquisition agreed on 2026-10-08 and 5.92x pro forma for the executive payment under the separation agreement dated 2026-10-11. The main downside is earnings falling back, through rebates, generic competition or supply problems, before the 2028 notes are refinanced.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C39
### Key findings

- Leverage has fallen but remains high, and it fell because earnings rose, not because debt fell. Total debt of USD 5,095 million is 6.47x last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 787 million, against 9.52x at FY2025, while debt itself is higher than at FY2025. EBITDA rose 47.38%, but USD 62 million of non-cash inventory step-up amortization sat in the FY2025 base, so the like-for-like rise is 32.05%. Because leverage is a ratio to one year of earnings, a return of EBITDA to its FY2025 level, a fall of 32.15%, would put total debt at 9.54x EBITDA.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18

- Interest cover is thin and the debt is mostly floating, so a rate shock and an earnings shock would arrive together. Accrued interest of USD 383 million takes 48.67% of EBITDA, cash interest cover was 1.41x in FY2025 and cannot be measured for the latest twelve months, and 72.12% of principal pays a floating rate with no interest rate swap or cap described in the filings. A rise of 100 bp adds about USD 36.53 million a year and takes cover from 2.05x to 1.88x; at the FY2025 earnings level cover would be 1.39x, or 1.27x after the same rise.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 102; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C19; calculation C20

- Cash conversion has turned positive but is still modest. Last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 252 million is 32.02% of EBITDA and 4.95% of total debt, after deficits of USD 198 million, USD 59 million and USD 66 million in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025. Trade receivables absorbed USD 496 million over those three years, more than the cumulative deficit of USD 323 million, so working capital, not the operating margin alone, decides whether the recovery in free cash flow lasts.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C28; calculation C29

- Liquidity is adequate for the next year, and the pressure sits in 2028 and 2031. Liquidity of USD 1,179 million is 3.30x the USD 357 million of fourth-quarter needs the issuer lists. Nothing but amortization is due before 2028, when USD 1,440 million falls due, 28.43% of principal and 1.83x EBITDA; USD 3,434 million, 67.80% of principal and 4.36x EBITDA, falls due in 2031. At the FY2025 earnings level those multiples would be 2.70x and 6.43x, so the 2028 notes are the first test of market access and the swing factor from 2027.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C45; calculation C43; calculation C41; calculation C44; calculation C42; calculation C21; calculation C22

- The revolver covenant is dormant and leaves room, but it is the only maintenance test and its headroom cannot be measured. The first lien net leverage test of 5.75x, stepping down to 5.50x, 5.25x and then 5.00x in later periods, applies only when revolver loans exceed 35% of the USD 800 million commitment, that is USD 280 million; USD 100 million is drawn, 12.50% of commitments, leaving USD 180 million before the test applies. Even if the USD 85 million acquisition and the USD 75 million executive payment were both drawn in full, loans would be USD 260 million, USD 20 million below the line, so the test is unlikely to apply in the fourth quarter but headroom beyond that is thin, and the issuer states compliance without a ratio so the result of a test is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C48; calculation C49; calculation C52; calculation C50; calculation C51

- Control by the parent is the main non-financial risk and has a direct liquidity link. Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, and part of its holding is pledged in a subsidiary for that subsidiary's 10.00% notes due 2032, in an amount the filings do not state. A change of control would let holders of both secured notes require repurchase at 101% of principal, USD 2,186.65 million before accrued interest or 1.85x liquidity; whether the credit agreement carries a comparable trigger is not stated, so the exposure of the largest debt, the term loan, is not established.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; calculation C46; calculation C47

- Pricing and rebates carry the revenue base and are exposed to regulation and generic entry. Net pricing contributed USD 128 million of the USD 317 million nine-month revenue increase and volume USD 139 million, but deductions from gross product sales rose 3.2 percentage points to 39.5% in 2025 and were 38.4% in the nine months of 2026 against 39.1% a year earlier, and a settlement with a generic maker allows entry for Lumify drops from 2027-06-30 or earlier. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a weak view is that the improvement is broad and cash-backed. EBITDA rose 47.38%, price and volume both contributed in Vision Care and Pharmaceuticals, accrued interest fell 11.76% in nine months, last-twelve-month free cash flow is USD 252 million after three years of deficits, total debt to EBITDA fell from 9.52x to 6.47x, liquidity covers the fourth-quarter needs by 3.30x, and nothing but amortization falls due before 2028. The parent has received no dividend since the listing, and the only large transfer to it in the filings, USD 2,429 million in 2022, is a dated event.

### Company description

Bausch + Lomb sells contact lenses and lens care, over-the-counter eye drops, prescription eye medicines and surgical equipment, implants and consumables. In 2025 Vision Care was 57.30% of revenue at USD 2,923 million, Pharmaceuticals 25.17% at USD 1,284 million and Surgical 17.53% at USD 894 million, and the United States and Puerto Rico supplied 49.91%. The analysis reads repeat purchase of lenses, solutions and drops by consumers and eye-care professionals as giving the revenue base visibility, which supports cash-flow predictability and debt service, but the ten largest products and franchises were 56% of revenue against 48% in 2023, so the visibility is concentrated.

Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, can elect the board and generally decides mergers, financing and dividend policy, and the issuer needs its written consent for certain significant actions until it holds less than 50% of the votes; the issuer qualifies for controlled-company exemptions from board-independence rules. ### Revenue durability and pricing power

The analysis reads revenue as mostly repeat consumer and clinician demand, and it is growing. In the nine months of 2026 over-the-counter products were USD 1,418 million and devices USD 1,521 million of USD 4,013 million, prescription pharmaceuticals USD 885 million and branded and other generics USD 175 million, and revenue rose 8.58%, or 7.28% excluding foreign exchange. Revenue also grew in each of the last three years, by 10.03% in 2023, 15.56% in 2024 and 6.47% in 2025, which supports the view that debt service rests on a growing base.

Price is a large part of that growth and is the most exposed. Net pricing added USD 128 million, volume USD 139 million and foreign exchange USD 48 million to the USD 317 million increase, so pricing was 40.38% of it, with Surgical pricing negative by USD 3 million and Surgical growth driven by volume. In the United States the Inflation Reduction Act requires manufacturers to pay Medicare rebates when prices rise faster than inflation, and deductions from gross product sales were 39.5% in 2025, up 3.2 percentage points, and were 38.4% in the nine months of 2026 against 39.1% a year earlier. A return of rebates would reduce net sales without any fall in volume, so revenue durability is moderate and sensitive to policy and to rebate contracts.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins have widened because costs were held while revenue grew, which is real operating leverage but not yet proven in a downturn. Nine-month selling, general and administrative cost rose 1.08% against revenue growth of 8.58%, cost of goods sold fell as a share of product sales to 37.4% from 41.1% on mix, currency, the end of the 2025 XIIDRA step-up and enVista recall effects and USD 15 million of tariff recoveries, and EBITDA margin rose 4.06 percentage points to 14.53% from 10.47% in FY2025. Selling, general and administrative cost was 43.80% of FY2025 revenue and the analysis treats it as largely fixed in the short run, so a revenue fall would cut margin faster than revenue.

The margin gain contains items that will not repeat and others that can be reversed. The USD 15 million of tariff recoveries and the end of the step-up are one-off, advertising and promotion fell because XIIDRA and MIEBO left their launch phase, and research and development rose 10% to USD 306 million in nine months. Reported EBITDA is also unadjusted: it is after other expense, net of USD 127 million over the last twelve months and after share-based compensation, so it is a conservative base. The levers available in a downturn are advertising and promotion, research and development timing and the cost programs the issuer says it may start, which together give some cost flexibility but not enough to hold margin if gross-to-net deductions rise.

Free cash flow is positive but only 32.02% of EBITDA, because interest, capital spending and working capital absorb the rest. ### Policy, economic and market factors

- Regulation and policy are material because they act directly on net price. Pricing is restricted by group purchasing contracts and by law: the Inflation Reduction Act requires Medicare rebates when prices rise faster than inflation, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act restricts funding of government health programs and may lower reimbursement, and a May 2025 executive order on most-favored-nation pricing may affect branded pharmaceutical products, while the issuer says the effect of expected health care changes is unclear, so policy can lower net sales and margin together across the United States, which is 49.91% of revenue, and regional spread elsewhere does not offset it.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 175; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322

- Tariffs and trade policy are material but have so far helped: the issuer recorded USD 15 million of recoveries of previously paid tariffs in nine months, a one-off gain that flatters margin, while it remains exposed to further tariffs on imported and exported product.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80

- Interest rates and currency are material through the debt. A majority of revenue and expense is in US dollars, but euro notes with principal of USD 765 million float on EURIBOR, a 1% move in foreign exchange rates changes equity by about USD 23 million, and cross-currency swaps of USD 1,000 million are described as hedging euro net investment, not interest rates. Russia, Ukraine and Belarus together were about 3% of revenue and the affected Middle East regions about 2%, a small and monitored exposure.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63

- Social and technology factors are not a primary credit driver on the filings supplied; the pipeline setback in July 2026, when the Phase 2 glaucoma neuroprotection trial missed its primary endpoint, removes upside but no cash flow that supports debt today.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61
### SWOT in credit terms

- Strengths: recovering EBITDA and positive free cash flow, liquidity of USD 1,179 million, no maturity before 2028 beyond amortization, three segments with growth in each, and price and volume both contributing to growth.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79
- Weaknesses: total debt at 6.47x EBITDA, accrued interest at 48.67% of EBITDA, 72.12% of principal at floating rates, control by a parent with a pledged stake, and ten products at 56% of revenue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C3

- Opportunities that would improve credit quality: the October 2028 notes have been callable since 2025-10-01 so they can be refinanced when markets allow, product mix has lowered cost of goods sold as a share of product sales and may continue to, and a distribution that ended parent control could remove the pledge and change-of-control exposure, although its terms are not known.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63

- Threats that would weaken it: generic entry for Lumify from 2027-06-30, rebates returning toward 2025 levels, a foreclosure on pledged shares, a rating action on the parent, an FDA escalation at the Tampa site and a debt-funded acquisition following the pending purchase.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is weak and improving, and the business profile is average. Scale is a support: revenue of USD 5,418 million over the last twelve months across three segments, with growth in each of the last three years. The constraints are leverage of 6.47x, cash interest cover of 1.41x in FY2025, a floating share of principal of 72.12%, free cash flow that was negative for three years until the last twelve months, and financial policy set by a controlling parent. The trend is up: EBITDA margin moved to 14.53% from 10.47%, and leverage fell from 9.52x to 6.47x, but both gains are one year old and partly reflect a depressed 2025 base.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3

The datapoints that would make the view more definitive are cash interest paid for 2026, an issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA and covenant ratio, the size of the pledged stake and the parent's leverage target, Lumify revenue, and the maintenance share of capital spending. Refinancing capacity is average: the issuer refinanced to 2030 and 2031 in June 2025 and January 2026, but USD 1,440 million falls due in 2028 and market access depends on earnings holding and on the parent's standing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

- Over the next one to two years, tailwinds are the earnings run-rate and lower interest: third-quarter operating income was USD 155 million against USD 95 million a year earlier and third-quarter interest expense was USD 95 million against USD 101 million. These support cover and cash generation if they persist.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

- Headwinds over the same period are the fourth-quarter cash calls of USD 357 million, the leadership transition, generic entry for Lumify from 2027-06-30, and an FDA warning letter for the Tampa site. Together they test whether free cash flow can fund the pending acquisition and the executive payment without drawing the revolver.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89

- Over three to five years, the debt profile decides the outcome: USD 1,440 million in 2028 and USD 3,434 million in 2031 must be refinanced from an earnings base of USD 787 million, or deleveraged from free cash flow of USD 252 million a year at the current rate. Health care pricing reform and generic competition are the sector headwinds that bear on that base; the issuer expects loss of exclusivity risk to be limited over five years but says it could change through patent challenges, settlements and at-risk launches.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 175; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

- Company-specific tailwinds are the maturing launches of XIIDRA and MIEBO and premium intraocular lens growth; the pipeline is a weaker support after the July 2026 Phase 2 setback, so growth must come from existing products.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80
### Downside scenario

The downside scenario is a fall of EBITDA back to its FY2025 level of USD 534 million, a drop of 32.15%, used as a reference point and not as a forecast. The initiating condition is a combination the filings make plausible: rebates and deductions return toward their 2025 level of 39.5% of gross product sales, Lumify faces generic entry from 2027-06-30 or earlier, and a supply or quality problem hits a single-source product. The first operating break is net revenue and margin, because pricing supplied 40.38% of nine-month growth and the analysis treats selling and administrative cost as largely fixed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C17; calculation C39

The financial transmission is through leverage and cover before liquidity. At the FY2025 earnings level total debt would be 9.54x EBITDA and accrued interest cover 1.39x, or 1.27x after a 100 bp rise, and the 2028 and 2031 maturities would be 2.70x and 6.43x EBITDA. FY2025 itself produced negative free cash flow of USD 66 million, so liquidity of USD 1,179 million would fund the shortfall for a long time and the revolver covenant, which applies only above USD 280 million of loans, would not bind unless loans rose by more than USD 180 million. The break therefore comes at refinancing: the 2028 notes would have to be replaced when EBITDA and cover are weakest, at a rate the market sets, and if the parent came under pressure, cash could be called on or pledged shares foreclosed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C48; calculation C49

Management levers are advertising and promotion, research and development timing, capital spending of USD 302 million over the last twelve months against capital commitments of USD 128 million, cost programs the issuer says it may start, the receivables facility and sale-leaseback of property, and the USD 666 million of revolver availability. These make liquidity distress unlikely before 2028 on the evidence, but they do not restore refinancing capacity at the downside leverage, and no default is assumed. Primary downside path: earnings fall back through rebates, generic entry or supply failure while the 2028 notes approach maturity and the parent holds control. The observable triggers are listed in the monitoring register.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 319
### Overall credit view

Overall, Bausch + Lomb presents an adequate business profile supported by a three-segment product range, repeat consumer and clinician demand and growth in each of the last three years, but credit quality is constrained by total debt of 6.47x EBITDA, thin interest cover, a mostly floating debt structure and control by a parent with a pledged stake. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but unproven: free cash flow of USD 252 million is one year old and rests on pricing and a depressed 2025 base. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings holding above USD 787 million, on rebates staying contained and on the parent not taking cash or losing control before the 2028 notes mature. Business quality compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers in eye health is not established, because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require cash interest paid for 2026, the credit agreement and covenant definitions, the size of the pledge and Lumify revenue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79
Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: a fall in earnings through rebates, generic entry or supply failure while leverage is high and the 2028 notes are refinanced under parent control.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Gaps

- Not supplied: cash interest paid for the nine months of 2026 and the latest twelve months. It limits the interest-cover conclusion, because the filings print cash interest only for full years, so cover is measured on accrued expense, which differed from cash paid by USD 41 million in FY2025. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the cash flow supplement of the next annual report.

- Not supplied: the credit agreement, its covenant definitions and any change-of-control or default terms for the term loan. It limits the conclusion on the revolver test and on the term loan's exposure to a change of control, because the largest debt, USD 2,788 million, has no stated change-of-control term and the covenant ratio cannot be calculated. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the executed credit agreement and a compliance certificate.

- Not supplied: peer leverage, credit ratings and market pricing. It limits the comparison of the financial profile with similar issuers, because the weak judgement rests on absolute metrics and the issuer's own history, not on a peer set. Severity Material; the action is to obtain peer, rating and bond price data.

- Not supplied: Lumify revenue and the acceleration clauses of the 2025 settlement. It limits the revenue-durability conclusion, because the loss of exclusivity from 2027-06-30 cannot be sized. Severity Material; the action is to obtain product revenue and the settlement terms.

- Not supplied: the size of the pledged parent shares and the parent's leverage target. It limits the conclusion on control and change-of-control risk, because the likelihood and timing of an ownership change cannot be judged. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the parent's filings.

- Not supplied: the split between maintenance and growth capital spending. It limits the assessment of capex flexibility, because the lever available in a downturn cannot be sized. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the issuer's capital allocation disclosure.

- Not supplied: management projections or guidance. It limits the downside and outlook sections, because the reference fall in EBITDA has no stated probability or timing. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain issuer guidance.

- Not supplied: an issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA. It limits the leverage conclusion, because reported EBITDA is after other expense, net of USD 127 million over the last twelve months and no issuer bridge exists. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the issuer's covenant earnings definition.
